name: Initial Results from the CHOOZ Long Baseline Reactor Neutrino Oscillation Experiment

significance.quote: we find (at 90% confidence level) no evidence for neutrino oscillations

summary.plain: First results from a kilometre-baseline reactor experiment: the antineutrino rate matched expectation, so there was no sign of electron-antineutrino disappearance. This excluded the atmospheric-neutrino mixing region for electron antineutrinos and showed the electron-flavour mixing angle was small.
summary.technical: Rate comparison of detected and expected positron events at ~1 km: no evidence (90 % CL) for oscillations in the anti-nu_e disappearance mode for delta m^2 > 0.9e-3 eV^2 at maximum mixing and sin^2(2 theta) > 0.18 at large delta m^2.

title: Initial Results from the CHOOZ Long Baseline Reactor Neutrino Oscillation Experiment
why_it_matters: Began the series of limits on the third mixing angle that Daya Bay, Double Chooz and RENO later turned into a measurement.
